title: Don't turn your back on calisthenics
summary: NH covers calisthenics for bodybuilding: it is an excellent base for novices and builds a strong upper body, but it is skill-based, hard to load progressively and weak for legs, especially the posterior chain. He praises training anywhere, its purity and its use as a gauge of muscle versus fat, tells how he lost his back development by dropping pull-ups, and ranks the best and worst bodyweight movements for hypertrophy.
claims: Calisthenics means any movement whose base pattern uses bodyweight, so an unloaded squat or lunge counts as much as a pull-up
Weighted and bodyweight calisthenics carry over to each other strongly, but the loaded versions do more for strength
Bodyweight training is limited for hypertrophy because the load is fixed; once you can do about 20 push-ups comfortably, add load (weighted push-ups, bench dips)
Harder lever variations such as planche push-ups mostly add technical difficulty, not muscular difficulty
Calisthenics, Olympic weightlifting and rings are skill sports, which is why athletes repeat the same movements to keep their technical rating high
Bodyweight training makes it hard to build quality volume and push intensity
Small legs in calisthenics athletes are a feature: a lighter lower body improves performance
For big legs, bodyweight options (pistols, shrimp squats, banded good mornings) are technical or inefficient; deadlifts and squats are better
Novices should learn to move their own body first; proprioception has to be built from the base
Starting with calisthenics gives easy, fun gains, carries over to barbell lifts and helps prevent injury
If you never feel your chest when benching, switch to push-ups for a while, get good at them, then go back to the bench
Starting with push-ups rather than the bench press lowers the risk of shoulder injury
Making calisthenics your pursuit means chasing performance, which may limit you if your goal is looks
Calisthenics athletes have well-developed quads but weak hamstrings, glutes and lower back because they never hip hinge, and extra posterior-chain mass hurts their performance
People who do calisthenics only for looks should admit it; they are bodybuilders, not calisthenics athletes, and pretending causes cognitive dissonance
Calisthenics movements are very good for upper-body hypertrophy
Calisthenics athletes stay very lean and light (often 160-170 lb) because performance is pound for pound, so beside bodybuilders they look small
Weighted pull-ups and inverted rows alone cover much of the back
Advanced bodyweight lifts take hundreds of hours of skill; every calisthenics lift can be replicated with weights more easily
Calisthenics lets you train anywhere, which is why its athletes are the most consistent he has seen
Resistance training most likely started as calisthenics; weight training is its natural evolution
Keep calisthenics in your program as a check: if your bench rises but push-ups regress, or your row rises but pull-ups drop, you are gaining fat, not muscle
Heavy lifters who suddenly do bodyweight work at high body fat often tear biceps or damage tendons
At 165-170 lb he could do 20 pull-ups; after bulking too much and dropping calisthenics for two years he could barely do 2
Buying into the bulking meme and bulking far too high for his frame left him fat, immobile and waddling
At the same 210 lb (495 vs 485 lb deadlift), the only difference between his flat back and his detailed back was two years of pull-ups
Pull-ups and inverted rows expose leg drive that people use when rowing
Novices can recover from daily full-body calisthenics because they cannot dig deep enough to do much damage
Done properly, pull-ups can be trained every day, even to failure, with continued progress; he did 40-80 pull-ups every training day
Dead hangs decompress the spine and shoulders and help lower back and shoulder pain; push-ups help rehab shoulders
Top 5 bodyweight moves for hypertrophy: pull-up, inverted row, push-up, leg raise, rings
Inverted rows can be trained 4 times a week; the upper back takes a lot of volume and neither pull-ups nor rows tax the lower back
Do leg raises on squat and deadlift days to decompress the spine and stretch the abs that were braced
Worst bodyweight moves for hypertrophy: muscle-ups, front levers, one-arm push-ups, dragon flags and planche, because they are skill tricks
He is weak at calisthenics but still does them; a hard movement is building muscle
